title: Attention Glance Index: Prefill Orchestration and Sparse KV Aliasing to Reduce Fragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: In paged attention workloads we observe high end-to-end tail latency driven by frequent small prefill wakes that thrash page residency and produce fragmented KV pages. Existing approaches (aggressive coalescing, long holding windows) either increase memory pressure or add latency for cold requests.

Goal: Introduce an 'Attention Glance Index' (AGI) — a lightweight per-tenant compact index that records inexpensive hints about recent token-span locality and kernel-affinity. Use AGI to: 1) inform sparse KV aliasing (map hot spans to alias slots rather than immediate full-page allocation), 2) coalesce micro-prefetch windows across nearby requests, and 3) orchestrate deferred decode interleaving to reduce simultaneous prefill spikes.

Proposal summary:
- Build a compact AGI stored as a small bitmap + hit counters per logical shard that is updated on prefill and decode completion.
- When a prefill request arrives, consult AGI to decide between: aliasing (pointing into an existing larger slot with offset metadata), in-place allocation, or a short deferred prefill (micro-delay to opportunistically coalesce with an incoming request).
- Add a Prefill Orchestrator module in the runtime that maintains a short window (configurable, default 8ms) for micro-coalescing prefill requests targeted at proximate token spans. The orchestrator also decides to interleave decodes from warm prefills with pending decode work to smooth GPU utilization.
- Kernel selection: extend kernel-adapter to expose a lightweight priority hint (ALIASED | COALESCED | FULL) which downstream kernel matcher uses to pick kernels optimized for aliased loads and sparse attention paths when possible.

Why this is different: AGI avoids full-page pinning by allowing safe alias references which reduce fragmentation growth. The micro-coalesce window reduces peak simultaneous prefill count without increasing steady-state latency for common workloads. Kernel hinting allows cheaper execution paths for aliased/sparse access patterns.

Metrics to track:
- 95th/99th prefill latency reduction (target: 20%/30%)
- Rate of page fragmentation/increase in free fragment count (target: -15%)
- Change in GPU occupancy jitter and decode throughput (target: stable or +5% throughput)
acceptance_criteria: AGI implemented with <1KB memory overhead per shard and unit tests covering update/read semantics
Prefill Orchestrator micro-coalesce window implemented and tunable via runtime flag
Kernel hint path exercised with a benchmark comparing aliased vs full allocation for representative models
End-to-end perf test: 99th prefill latency reduced by >=20% on pinned benchmark, fragment growth rate down by >=10% over 72-hour run
Canary rollout plan documented and automated (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback metric thresholds
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after the 2026-Q1 perf retro. Spike showed repeated small prefills from conversational workloads cause fragmentation to grow linearly over 48h.

2026-02-22 Marco Chen: Spike results look promising. Implemented a prototype AGI using an LRU-bitset. Observed 12% reduction in fragment churn in synthetic workload (local), added micro-coalesce timer as a knob.
2026-03-01 Review by Priya Nair (SRE): Concern about cross-tenant alias safety during eviction. We agreed on a short-lived alias lease plus verification on decode; added lease expiry tests.
2026-03-04 Design review: Decided NOT to modify page format on-disk; AGI will store alias metadata in runtime-only metadata layer to keep backward compatibility for migrations.
2026-03-08 Engineering update: Kernel adapter hook added (ALIASED | COALESCED | FULL). Benchmarks show a 6% reduce in token decode time for aliased-path in T5-like model with long contexts.

2026-03-12 Marco Chen: Integration tests failing for a minority tenant under heavy eviction; root cause is alias lease renewal race. Added jitter and centralized lease renewal gate to Prefill Orchestrator; new tests added.
2026-03-12 QA: Added end-to-end 72h run to perf CI; will start canary once stability threshold met.
implementation_notes: AGI structure: 64-bit fingerprint + 8-bit recency counter per entry, ring-buffer sized to ~128 entries per shard (tunable)
Alias semantics: alias entry stores (target_page_id, offset, lease_expiry_ts). On decode, runtime verifies that the alias maps to resident page; if missing, fallback to normal prefill path.
Prefill Orchestrator: single-threaded event loop per-node that groups prefill intents by shard and token-span proximity, emits coalesced prefill jobs to allocator
Kernel hinting: add small enum to request header and update kernel-selector scoring to prefer sparse-kernel variants when ALIASED or COALESCED
Safety: alias leases are short (default 200ms) and renewals require ownership token to avoid stale cross-tenant pointers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Alias pointer becomes stale during eviction causing decode fallback storms. Mitigation: immediate fallback path and rate limit fallbacks with exponential backoff
Risk: Micro-coalesce window increases median latency for cold paths. Mitigation: make window configurable and small default (8ms), opt-out for P0 latency customers
Risk: Additional metadata increases GC pressure in control plane. Mitigation: compact AGI representation and periodic vacuum job
